levelScaling._comment: How levels count in combat (Model P). Stats and the damage formula's level term use pivot x (level / pivot)^exponent instead of the level itself; at the pivot the two agree, below it a level counts a little more, above it a little less (level 50 fights like 42, level 100 like 71). Shown levels, XP, evolution and move learning keep the real level.

party._xpComment: XP to the next level = xpBase + xpPerLevel*L + xpPerLevelSq*L^2; a knockout pays xpKoBase + xpKoPerLevel*L (up to double against higher levels), times xpEliteMultiplier for elite wilds and xpBossMultiplier for the stronger encounters (spawns.json strong). An even fight is worth about a level and a quarter early on, one level around level 25 and under a level by level 40 (about half the old pace). The partner out with the lead takes half; Pokémon in their balls take benchShare. A catch gives the lead catchXpShare of a knockout.
party._fieldComment: Every trainer has at most fieldLimit Pokémon out at once (the first ones in party order that can fight); the rest wait in their balls and come out as others faint or on a swap.

wild._calmComment: Round every trainer's starting point the wilds keep their land's base levels: no centre bonus within calmTiles[0] tiles of a start, the full bonus from calmTiles[1].
wild._eliteComment: eliteChance of wild spawns are elites: eliteLevels more levels (evolved if that passes an evolution), marked with a gold star.
wild._alphaComment: Within alphaRadius tiles of the Shadow Crystal, alphaChance of wild spawns are Alphas: alphaLevelBonus levels above the wilds around them (at most alphaLevelMax), fully evolved, drawn alphaScale times bigger, worth xpAlphaMultiplier XP. Elsewhere levels climb by up to centerLevelBonus toward the crystal, spread by centerLevelSpread.
wild._shinyComment: shinyChance: the chance any wild Pokemon is shiny (every land spawn, every stronger encounter, every fishing bite), if its species has shiny colours. 0.01 (1 in 100) gives about three shinies among a match's 310 or so wild Pokemon and fishing bites, so most matches have one or two somewhere, and a trainer who meets 40-60 wilds sees one about every other match. Alphas use shinyChance x alphaShinyMultiplier. A match's shiny boost (server events) multiplies both, once. Events with their own chosen odds (the forest stranger's Zoroark, spawns.json events) do not use this.

trainers._speedComment: speed: how fast trainers walk to their spots in a one-on-one battle. Out on the map computer trainers walk at the player's pace (player.speedTilesPerSec), start like a new player (one starter rolled from the new-player tiers, the player's level, bag and money) and play by the same rules (src/sim/bot.ts).
trainers._huntComment: Computer trainers hunt the wild Pokemon within huntRange tiles that their team beats comfortably (src/sim/ai.ts fightMargin: the matchup in HP, moves, types and stats, not level alone; Alphas and land bosses only with a clear edge), catch the ones worth a slot, and go back to an outpost within healTripRange tiles when worn down (party HP at or under huntHpFraction, or half the team fainted). Passing a healer, they ask for a heal only when under three quarters HP or someone fainted.
trainers._viewComment: huntRange: how far a computer trainer notices wild Pokémon, about what a player sees on screen (it explores to find more).

battle._channelComment: Channelled beams: these moves keep firing for channel.seconds after they go off, a pulse every channel.tick seconds, and the user steers the beam (the player with the cursor, others at their target) turning at most channel.turnDegPerSec. The user stands still meanwhile. The whole channel deals powerMult x the move's power, spread over the pulses.
battle._lungeComment: Contact moves (physical, one target, not thrown: Tackle, Bite, Close Combat...) lunge: the user rushes at its target at speed tiles a second (times its Speed multiplier and the move's dash), covering at most maxTiles (times dash) in at most maxSeconds, following a target that moves, and strikes on arrival. It lands only if the two bodies are then touching (data.contactReach: their radii plus reachSlack): a lunge stopped by a wall, or a target that got away, is a miss. A contact hit or a slam's landing shoves the target knockTiles (times power / 80 within knockScale, times the move's knock) unless it is a boss, a legend, an Alpha, a Shadow Pokémon, mid-leap or much bigger than the attacker; walls stop the shove.
battle._damageScaleComment: Every hit is scaled by damageScale so fights last a few exchanges instead of two or three moves.
battle._statusComment: poison ticks poisonDamageFraction of max HP every 2 s until cured (Poison and Steel types are immune); freeze stops a Pokémon for freezeSeconds (a Fire hit thaws it; Ice and Fire types are immune); confusion lasts confusionSeconds and sends each move off in a random direction confusionMissChance of the time.
battle._speedComment: Movement speed from the Speed stat: a Pokémon with base Speed slowBase moves at slowMult of the normal pace, one with fastBase at fastMult, in a straight line between (clamped to that range). Speed stages add stagePerStep each (Agility), paralysis multiplies by paralysisSpeed. Following its trainer a Pokémon never drops below followFloor tiles a second when hurrying, so slow ones still keep up.

items._startingKitComment: What every trainer (you and every rival) carries at the start of a match.
items._storageComment: Every town has a storage chest beside its healer. They share one store per trainer (storageSlots slots, each stacking any number of one item) that keeps items safe when you are wiped out.
items._alphaMegaStoneComment: The chance an Alpha of a Mega-capable line drops its Mega Stone (item balls also hold one now and then, loot.json).

styler._comment: Capture Styler: hold C and draw loops round a wild Pokémon. It needs baseLoops + 1 per perLevel levels (+eliteLoops for elites, +bossLoops for the stronger encounters and Alphas, at most maxLoops). A full set calms it for calmSeconds: it stops fighting and every ball thrown at it counts catchMultiplier times. The line reaches maxRange tiles from the trainer; if the Pokémon runs through the line it breaks and one loop is lost.

dodge._comment: Space (when nothing is in reach to talk to or pick up) dashes your lead dashTiles in the direction you move (or face) over dashSeconds; hits that land in the first safeSeconds miss. Rivals in one-on-one battles dodge telegraphed moves aiChance of the time.

duel._finalShowdownComment: true pulls the last two trainers to the Shadow Crystal's arena for a one-on-one final; false lets them find each other.
duel._comment: One-on-one trainer battles: two trainers within startRange (and in sight) recall their parties and send out one Pokémon each. Trainers step apart to standGap; leads come out sendOut tiles in front; the fight stays within arenaRadius of the middle. The player steers the lead at monSpeed and picks every move (auto-battle is off in battles). A rival picks its next Pokémon after aiPickSeconds. A player has playerPickSeconds to choose theirs; after that the first one able in party order comes out by itself, so an idle or disconnected player can not hold a battle open. If both sides run out at once, the battle ends with no winner. zoom is the camera zoom while the player battles.

outpost._centerCost: Poké Dollars per heal at the Crystal Healer, the paid healer just south of the centre arena (0 removes it).

visitors._comment: hoopaChance: the share of matches Hoopa appears in (add ?hoopa=1 to the address, or turn on tester mode with ?dev=1, to force it).
visitors._portalComment: Hoopa's portal legendary comes through at your best level + portalLevelOver, at least portalLevelMin (at most 100). Legendaries in a bout can be caught with balls at legendCatchScale of the ball's usual rate, or join you when worn to their last HP.

shadowLugia._comment: Once Tide Lake is inside the darkness, a Super Rod cast there draws Shadow Lugia (once a match): a long wait, then a hook window of biteWindow seconds. It fights at level (a full-strength Lv 100), with hpMult times its HP like every legendary and damageScale on its hits; its beam lasts beamSeconds and turns at beamTurnScale of the usual rate. Shadow Storm (a ring of dark gusts) every stormEvery[phase] seconds. Balls bounce off: under snagBelow of its HP a Snag Machine takes it; worn to nothing or winning the bout, it vanishes.

riding._comment: V rides (kind ride) or flies on (kind fly) the first mount in the party. seat: where the rider sits, as a fraction of the mount's body height above the ground; back: how far toward the tail the rider sits in side views (fraction of body width); scale: draw the mount bigger while ridden (a bird big enough to carry a trainer). Flying lifts the mount flyLift tiles, crosses water and keeps out of trainer battles.
riding._mountsComment: Mounts and their saddle points. seat: rider height as a fraction of body height (side views); seatDown/seatUp override it facing the camera and away; back: toward the tail in side views; scale: the mount draws this much bigger while ridden. Latios, Raikou, Flygon and Torterra carry trainers.

eggs._comment: The Breeder's Eggs (src/sim/townsfolk.ts) sit in party slots and hatch after hatchSteps tiles walked with them (counted on the server from the trainer's real movement; standing still or walking into a wall adds nothing). mythicalChance of Eggs hold a small Mythical Pokemon (townsfolk.ts MYTHICAL_EGGS) instead of one of the Breeder's lines.

respawn._comment: A trainer whose last Pokémon falls to a wild Pokémon comes back after baseSeconds + perMinute for each minute played (up to maxSeconds), at an outpost, with the party healed and every item lost (dropped where they fell). No respawns once the final showdown starts.

darkness._comment: Every pulseSeconds the safe circle shrinks to the next radius; the darkness creeps in at sweepTilesPerSecond (a trainer walks about 4.8).
darkness._stormMaskComment: A Storm Mask in the bag (the Wandering Merchant sells one in stormMaskChance of matches): that trainer's Pokémon take stormMaskSeconds in the darkness to fall asleep instead of drowsySeconds.
darkness._trainerComment: Trainers last trainerToleranceScale times as long as their Pokemon in the storm (16 s, or 8 minutes with a Storm Mask), then pass out: Darkrai drags them into the shadows and they are out of the match. Their exposure drains twice as fast outside the storm.

sizes._comment: Pokémon are drawn to their Pokédex height against the trainers: a trainer sprite's body (trainerPx art pixels) stands trainerHeightM tall. Pokémon under smallFloorM are drawn on a ramp from smallBaseM (at 0 m) up to smallFloorM, so small ones stay readable and still smaller than bigger ones; no body is drawn under minDrawnM tall (long, coiled ones included). Giants are capped at maxShownM (Wailord). Species whose Pokedex figure is a length say along: length, and serpents drawn coiled scale it by coil.
